correctness.rationale: Every ideal is represented as either the empty ideal or a root-containing vector of arm-prefix lengths. The proof establishes an exact Littlestone game recurrence: the root query isolates the empty ideal; an arm threshold splits into a rectangular product and a smaller augmented product. Product threshold dimensions are additive, with each coordinate contributing floor(log2 b_i). Induction shows the augmented dimension is one larger iff all b_i equal 2^(a_i+1)-1; the equality query j=2^a-1 has both children of baseline rank. This covers all nonnegative numbers of arms, all positive lengths, and boundaries including m=0. A standalone exact version-space program checked the formula and ideal counts for 183 small rooted-spider isomorphism types (sum of vertices <=13). The finite computation is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected studies concern general Littlestone-dimension closure bounds, direct-product additivity, and enumeration of finite-poset ideals. These ingredients do not entail the precise iff Mersenne criterion for the change caused by one extra empty-ideal hypothesis. Prior accessible work on two-row grid-poset ideals gives a recurrence for a structurally different partial order; it does not imply the closed rooted-spider formula. Semantic searches found no exact or stronger coverage. Residual risk of unindexed prior art is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The poset ideal-membership class is natural in finite order theory and online prediction. A complete closed formula holds for every arm-count and every arm length, with a sharp structural equality criterion characterizing when adding a single root-negative empty ideal increases the mistake bound. The exceptional phenomenon persists in arbitrarily large rooted spiders (for example all arms of length two), and fails in closely neighboring length vectors. This is an interpretable structural online-rank result, not a renaming, arbitrary finite slice, or a re-enumeration of already known ideal counts.
